title: Clerk-reachable acceptance criteria are marked accountBound and skip with a stable-coded reason when Clerk is unreachable
asA: operator running the project's runtime-verify suite in a CI environment without Clerk reachability
iWant: the acceptance criteria that depend on a live Clerk development instance to skip with a documented reason rather than pass on a fake
soThat: the ship gate does not falsely record identity behaviour as verified when the verification path never actually ran

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every test case bound to an AC whose runtime observability requires a live Clerk session (AC-9101-1, AC-9101-2, AC-9101-3, AC-9103-1, AC-9103-2, AC-9103-3, AC-9107-1, AC-9107-2, AC-9109-2) carries an `accountBound` marker on the test harness.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the project's runtime-verify test harness at manifest-generation time
acceptanceCriteria.when: the harness enumerates test cases and their bound ACs
acceptanceCriteria.then: every TC bound to one of the enumerated ACs above has the `accountBound` marker set; TCs bound to other ACs (source-tree scans, in-process principal-shape assertions, adapter unit-shaped checks) do not carry the marker

acceptanceCriteria.description: A runtime-verify run against a target without Clerk reachability records the accountBound TCs as skipped with the stable-coded reason `AUTH_CLERK_UNREACHABLE`, not as passed.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a runtime-verify run configured with no reachable Clerk publishable/secret keys or with Clerk's session-verification surface unreachable
acceptanceCriteria.then: every accountBound TC records outcome `skipped` with reason field equal to `AUTH_CLERK_UNREACHABLE`; the ship gate report flags the skipped set; the run's overall status reflects the skip rather than a pass
